key_insight: Agentic coding workflows spend a large share of tokens on orchestration (prompts, tool calls, and iterative debugging) rather than the final code output, and token consumption can be predicted reasonably well from task and agent-level features before execution.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of systematic understanding and forecasting of where and how tokens are consumed by AI agents in coding tasks, enabling cost-aware model/agent selection and pipeline optimization.
method: Curate and analyze a dataset of agentic coding trajectories to break down token usage by stage (prompting, tool calls, model responses, retries, etc.).
Compare token-efficiency across models and agent designs to identify high-cost components and model-level tradeoffs.
Train lightweight predictors using task/agent features (e.g., problem size, tool usage, agent loop counts) to forecast token consumption before task execution.
impact: Provides practitioners with actionable insights and pre-run cost estimates to choose more token-efficient models, redesign agent workflows, and reduce operational costs without sacrificing task performance.
visual_elements: Stacked pie/bar chart showing token breakdown by component (prompt, tool calls, model replies, retries)
Grouped bar chart comparing total tokens used by different LLM models and agent styles
Pipeline flow diagram annotated with token hotspots (where tokens concentrate across agent steps)
Scatter plot of predicted vs. actual token usage with an error band to show prediction reliability
paper_title: How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks
paper_authors: Longju Bai, Zhemin Huang, Xingyao Wang, Jiao Sun, Rada Mihalcea
